rounds.name: Technical Interview
must_do: Never accept a definition — immediately ask for an example, or where they used it in code
Go two or three layers deep on one topic before moving to the next
If it sounds memorised, go straight to an application question
Have them write code on paper once — pseudo-code is fine

rounds.name: Project & Resume Deep-Dive
must_do: Pick the project at the top of the resume
Not what was built — ask what THEY personally wrote
Take one design choice and ask why that, and why not the alternative
Ask what happens when it fails — push on the failure mode
If the answers stay vague, say you are not convinced — politely, but plainly

rounds.name: Managerial Round (MR)

rounds.name: HR Round
must_do: Catch the rehearsed answer — everyone says that, ask for their own example
Follow up on the weakness: what did they actually do about it?

rounds.name: Online Assessment (2 DSA + Work Style + Work Simulation)
rounds.note: The app does not simulate this — it happens on a coding platform.

rounds.name: Technical 1 — DSA
must_do: Ask for the approach before any code — start with how they would think about it
Once brute force arrives, ask them to optimise it; never hand over the solution
Make them state both time and space complexity
Raise one edge case they have missed
Slip one Leadership Principle behavioral question into the middle of the round

rounds.name: Technical 2 — DSA + Design-lite

Raise one edge case they have missed
Add a small design angle: how would this run for a million users
